GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
DEPARTMENT OF PHARMACEUTICALS 
 
LOK  SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 3229 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 16th  March,  2021 
 
Shortage of Medicines 
 
3229.  SHRIMATI SUMALATHA AMBAREESH:  
SHRI NALIN KUMAR KATEEL:  
 
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether it is a fact that except for some medicines, there is an acute shortage of medicines 
in Janaushadhi Kendras in most of the States;  
(b) if so, the details thereof; and  
(c)whether the Government has any such system which can reflect centre -wise and medicine-
wise shortage and if so, the details thereof? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
(SHRI D.V. SADANANADA GOWDA) 
 
(a) & (b) Bureau of Pharma PSUs of India (BPPI), the implementing agency of Pradhan Mantri 
Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) makes regular efforts for making all the drugs in its 
product basket available to the consumers through its more than 7,500 Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya 
Janaushadhi Kendras (PMBJKs). Sometimes, some drugs could not be made available due to 
non-receipt of valid bids for the particular drug/non -supply by a vendor. Floating tenders for 
required medicines are being issued regularly to avoid any stock-out situation. 
 
(c)   BPPI has implemented IT enabled SAP based forecasting system for efficient inventory 
management. This system forecasts the demand of medicines, take real -time orders from Jan 
Aushadhi Kendras, identify purchase level and tracks the delivery of purchase  orders issued. 
The system ensures that medicines are purchased on right time and made available to Kendras 
timely.

-

(b) the number of CPSUs reported as profit making as well as those incurring losses during

(c) whether the Government has assessed the reasons for these undertakings incurring losses 
constantly; and 
(d) if so, the action plan prepared to address these problems?

MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEAVY INDUSTRIES AND PUBLIC ENTERPRISES

(a) and (b) There are 366 Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) in the country as on 31st 
March, 2020 . The State/UT-wise list of CPSEs is at Annexure . There are 119 CPSEs 
continuously in profit for last 5 years and 30 CPSEs continuously in losses for last 5 years. 
(c) and (d) CPSEs function under the administrative control of respective 
Ministries/Departments. All matters relating to revival/ restructuring/closure of  CPSEs are 
dealt by the concerned administrative Ministries/ Departments. The concerned administrative 
Ministries/Departments also formulate revival/restructuring plans for such CPSEs on a case -
to-case basis and after obtaining the approval of competent au thority implement the plan.  
The Department of Public Enterprises (DPE) has issued guidelines on 29.10.2015 for 
“Streamlining the mechanism for revival and restructuring of sick/ incipient sick and weak 
CPSEs. As per the guidelines, the administrative Mini stries/ Departments are responsible to 
monitor the sickness of CPSEs and identify the sick/incipient sick/weak CPSEs functioning 
under their control based on the performance and take timely redressal measures.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
 MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3237 
ANSWERED ON 16TH MARCH, 2021 
  
COLD CHAIN FACILITIES 
 
3237. SHRI HEMANT TUKARAM GODSE; 
 
  Will the Minister of  FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the capacity of cold storage and cold chains available in the country are  
adequate to meet the demand for storing perishable commodities like fruits and 
vegetables; and 
 
(b) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
  
 
ANSWER 
 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES  
(SHRI RAMESWAR TELI) 
  
(a) & (b): The study on All India Cold-chain Infrastructure Capacity (AICIC-2015) conducted 
by NABCONS reported that 35 million tones cold storage capacity is required against the 
existing capacity of 32 million tones.  
   
Though the Government does not setup such storage facilities at its own, it has been 
making efforts towards bridging the gap between demand and supply. Government is extending 
financial support for setting of such facilities through its scheme namely “Mission for Integrated 
Development of Horticulture (MIDH)” of the Department of Agriculture,  Cooperation & 
Farmers Welfare (DoAC &FW) and "Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojna (PMKSY)" of the 
Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI).  
  
These schemes are demand/entrepreneur -driven from among entrepreneurs, private 
companies, cooperatives, farmers group etc.

3240. SHRI ARVIND GANPAT SAWANT:

SHRI DHANUSH M. KUMAR:  
SHRI SELVAM G.:

d`f"k vkSj fdlku dY;k.k ea=h be pleased to state:

(b) whether ICAR has carried out research and d eveloped several flood and drought

availability of new rice varieties;

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
LOK  SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3242 
  ANSWERED ON 16.03.2021 
  
REVERSE MIGRATION 
 
3242.  SHRIMATI POONAM MAHAJAN: 
MS. RAMYA HARIDAS: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the current status of reverse migration from c ity to village/district during the last five 
years; 
(b)  the States and cities which witnessed the larg est number of reverse migration and the 
reasons of this reverse migration; 
(c)  whether these migrated people get jobs, if so,  the sector in which they are employed and 
their average wages per day; 
(d)  the percentage of unemployment within reverse migration; and 
(e)  whether the Government has drawn plans to equi p these unemployed battery of youth 
with job oriented skills and if so, the details of the courses offered? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRI NARENDRA SINGH TOMAR) 
 
(a) & (b)  Migration of workers from one State to anoth er State is a continuous process and the 
migrant workers keep on moving from one State to ot her States in search of work. In regard to 
reverse migration, Ministry of Labour & Employment has informed that as reported by the 
States/UTs, during the Covid-19 lockdown situation,  a total of 1,14,30,968 inter-state migrant 
workers returned to their home states. State-wise b reak up is enclosed at the Annexure . Further, 
it has been informed by Ministry of Labour & Employ ment that most of reverse migrants have 
gone back to their original or other workplaces and  engaged themselves in productive 
employment. 
 
(c)  to (e)  Government has taken several measures post  COVID-19 situation to provide relief to 
the people in rural areas, including the reverse mi grants people in all States/UTs. Ministry of 
Finance, Government of India, on 26th March 2020, a nnounced relief package under Pradhan 
Mantri Garib Kalyan Yojana (PMGKY) for the poor to help them fight the battle against Corona 
Virus. The relief package announced includes, inter-alia:  
i. One-time ex-gratia payment of Rs 500 per month for 3 months (April, May and June 2020) 
to women Jan Dhan Account holders. In pursuance of this, Ministry of Rural Development 
(MoRD) implemented the scheme of relief package of one-time ex-gratia payment of       
Rs 500 per month for 3 months (April, May and June 2020) to women Jan Dhan Account 
holders through various Banks. A total of Rs. 30956 .97 crores has been released towards 
direct benefit transfers to 20.64 crore Women benef iciaries of Jan Dhan account holders 
under Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) @ Rs. 500/- each for three months.  

 
ii. Ex-gratia of Rs.1000 in two instalments (Rs.500/- e ach) to the existing old age, widow and 
disabled/Divyangjan beneficiaries of the schemes of  National Social Assistance 
Programme(NSAP).  A total of Rs. 2814.50 crore as e x-gratia was released in two tranches 
in April and May, 2020 to States/UTs under PMGKY fo r the existing 282 lakh 
beneficiaries of NSAP schemes.  
 
iii. Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (Mahatma Gandhi NREGA) 
wage rate revised w.e.f. 1.4.2020 with average wage  rate increase of Rs.20 over the wage 
rate of 2019-20. 
 
iv. The collateral free credit limit for the Self Help Group(SHG) members under National 
Rural Livelihood Scheme (NRLM) enhanced from Rs.10 lakh to Rs. 20 lakh. 
 
 Apart from this, Government of India launched the Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan 
(GKRA) on 20 
th  June, 2020 for a period of 125 days to boost emplo yment and livelihood 
opportunities for returnee migrant workers and simi larly affected citizens in rural area, in the 
wake of COVID-19 pandemic with resource envelop of Rs. 50,000 crore. The objectives of the 
Abhiyaan were to provide immediate employment & livelihood opportunities to the distressed, to 
saturate the villages with public infrastructure an d creation of livelihood assets to boost the 
income generation activities and enhance long term livelihood opportunities by giving focus on 
25 works in 116 selected districts across 6 States of Bihar, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, 
Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh. The Abhiyaan is a conv ergent effort of ongoing 25 schemes of 12 
Ministries/ Department of Central Government. More than 50 crore man-days of employment 
was created under the Abhiyaan with an expenditure of Rs. 39292.81 crore. 
 Four schemes of the MoRD namely, Mahatma Gandhi Na tional Rural Employment 
Guarantee Scheme (Mahatma Gandhi NREGS), Pradhan Ma ntriAwaasYojana- Gramin (PMAY-
G), Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) and Sh yama Prasad Mukherjee RURBAN 
Mission (SPMRM) have been identified under the GKRA . The achievement in this regard is as 
under:  
i. PMAY-G has sanctioned a total of 770522 houses and completed 481210 houses with a 
total expenditure of Rs.5618.19 crore.  
ii. Under PMGSY, as against the target of Rs. 2902 cror e, an expenditure of Rs. 1529 crore 
has been incurred as on 30.11.2020.  
iii. Under SPMRM, the development works in 47 Rurban clu sters under GKRA have been 
implemented with fast pace for providing employment  and livelihood opportunities to the 
rural citizens. During the abhiyaan period, 13494 w orks have been completed against the 
target of 13886 which is 97% of overall physical ta rget and Rs. 693.55 crore expenditure 
(including convergence expenditure) has been made which is 87% of financial targets taken 
by SPMRM under GKRA. 
 
 Other major steps taken by the MoRD under various schemes during the outbreak of 
Covid-19 for expeditious socio- economic development in rural areas are listed below: 
i. Mahatma Gandhi NREGS which is a demand driven wage employment programme 
provides at least one hundred days of guaranteed wage employment in every financial year 
is to every rural household whose adult members vol unteer to do unskilled manual work. 
During FY 2020-21 (upto 11.03.2021), more than 363 crore person-days have been 
generated, which is approximately 44% more than the  employment generated during the 
same period in FY 2019-20 and  more than 1.61 crore  new job cards have been issued. 
Government has enhanced the allocation under Mahatm a Gandhi NREGA for Financial 
Year 2020-21 from BE Rs. 61,500 crore to Rs.1,11,500 crore.  

 
ii. PMAY-G aims to provide assistance to eligible rural  households for construction of 2.95 
Crore Pucca houses with basic amenities to achieve the objective of “Housing for All” by 
2022. In the current FY, 36.38 lakh houses have bee n sanctioned and 28.45 lakh houses 
have been completed in PMAY-G and 0.64 lakhs in Ind ira Awaas Yojana (IAY) with an 
expenditure of Rs.39195 crore.  
 
iii. PMGSY was launched in the year 2000 as a measure to wards alleviation of poverty in 
rural areas by providing access to basic services t o the rural population by providing them 
good quality roads. During the period of COVID stat es were directed to accelerate the 
pace of works so as to create more employment oppor tunities and boost rural economy. 
Under PMGSY, 25,943 Kms. of road length has been co mpleted in 2020-21 and 
expenditure of Rs. 18,923 Cr. Incurred during this financial year.  
 
iv. SPMRM is a unique programme, designed to deliver ca talytic interventions to rural areas 
on the threshold of growth. 300 Rurban Clusters wit h thematic economic growth points, 
are being developed across the country under this M ission. The Ministry had issued an 
advisory to the States/UTs regarding modification i n existing projects/works proposed in 
DPR of cluster due to Covid-19 pandemic and to incl ude more economic activities in 
order to reboot the rural economy. Cluster wise con sultations have been convened with 
PRI members, SHG representatives as well as State a nd district functionaries to identify 
issues and suggestions with respect to further impr oving the on-ground implementation of 
the Mission. Under SPMRM, a total expenditure Rs. 3 089 Cr. including convergence 
funds and critical gap funds has been incurred during financial year 2020-21.  
 
v. Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelih oods Mission(DAY-NRLM) aims 
to reduce poverty by organizing the rural poor wome n into Self Help Groups (SHGs), and 
continuously nurturing and supporting them to take economic activities till they attain 
appreciable increase in income over a period of tim e. During the year 2020-21 (till Jan 
2021), the Ministry of Rural Development under DAY- NRLM facilitated women Self 
Help Groups to leverage credit of Rs 56417 Crores f rom formal banking system for 
investing for continuation of their exiting economi c ventures and also acquire new 
productive assets to start new enterprises.  
 
vi. There are two other skill development programmes fo r rural poor youth under DAY-
NRLM, namely, Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushaly a Yojana (DDU-GKY), and 
Rural Self Employment Training Institutes (RSETIs).   Both these schemes are aimed at 
increasing employability of rural poor youth either  for wage or self-employment. After 
unlock orders and opening of training centres, under DDU-GKY a total of 9986 candidates 
have been trained and 36933 candidates have been pl aced in jobs during the current 
financial year 2020-21 (upto December, 2020). Under  RSETI a total of 111367 candidates 
have been trained and 93874 candidates have been se ttled during the current Financial 
Year 2020-21(upto December, 2020).  
 
Apart for the above mentioned schemes/programmes of  Ministry of Rural Development, major 
schemes/programmes of other Ministries/departments for skill development and employment 
generation which provide employment opportunities a nd employability to the rural youth 
including the reverse migrants are as under- 
 
 

 
i. PRADHAN MANTRI KAUSHAL VIKAS YOJANA - The Ministry of Skill 
Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) had launche d Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas 
Yojana (PMKVY) in the year 2015. The objective of t his Skill Certification Scheme is to 
enable a large number of Indian Youth to take up in dustry-relevant skill training that will 
help them in securing a better livelihood. Individu als with prior learning experience or 
skills will also be assessed and certified under th e Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) 
component of the Scheme. RPL mainly focuses on the individuals engaged in unregulated 
sectors.  The objectives of RPL are primarily three -fold: (i) to align the competencies of 
the un-regulated workforce of the country to the st andardized National Skills Qualification 
Framework (NSQF), (ii) to enhance the career/employ ability opportunities of an individual 
as well as provide alternative routes to higher edu cation and (iii) to provide opportunities 
for reducing inequalities based on forms of knowledge over others.  
 
ii. PRIME MINISTER’S EMPLOYMENT GENERATION PROGRAMME (P MEGP)-
The Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises h as been implementing a credit-
linked subsidy programme named Prime Minister’s Emp loyment Generation Programme 
(PMEGP) since 2008-09 with Khadi and Village Indust ries Commission (KVIC) as nodal 
agency at the national level for generating employm ent in the country by setting up of 
micro-enterprises in the non-farm sector by helping  traditional artisans and unemployed 
youth.

CENTRE-STATE RELATIONS 
 
3245.  SHRI NALIN KUMAR KATEEL: 
  SHRIMATI SUMALATHA AMBAREESH: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the salient features of the report submitted by the Commission on 
Centre- State Relations headed by Justice Punchhi in 2010? 
 
(b) whether any consultation process between Union and the States via 
Inter-State Council for legislation on concurrent subjects have started 
during last three years? 
 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(d) whether any Commission would be appointed to revisit distribution of 
Centre-State powers in view of objections raised by various States on 
the legislations relating to electricity, agriculture etc. and if so, the 
details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
 
(a) : The Commission submitted its report in 2010 in 7 Volumes containing

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY & DAIRYING 
DEPARTMENT OF ANIMAL HUSBANDRY & DAIRYING  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3247 
TO BE ANSWERED ON  16TH MARCH, 2021 
 
“MIGRATORY BIRDS AS SOURCE OF AVIAN INFLUENZA” 
 
3247.SHRI RAJENDRA DHEDYA GAVIT:  SHRI CHANDRA SEKHAR SAHU: SHRI 
SANJAY SADASHIVRAO  MANDLIK: SHRI SHRIRANG APPA BARNE: SHRI RAVI 
KISHAN: SHRI BIDYUT BARAN MAHATO: SHRI SUBRAT PATHAK:  SHRI SUDHEER 
GUPTA: 
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
  मत्स्यपाऱन, पशुपाऱन और डेयरी मंत्री 
 be pleased to state: 
 
a)  whether migratory birds are the potential source of Avia Influenza in the country;  
b)  if so, the number of migratory birds annually visiting in various States including the State of 
Maharashtra, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha;  
c)  whether any study has so far been conducted in this regard, if so, the details in this regards;  
d)  the details of States covered for Avian Influenza Test at RDDL (ER), Kolkata and at    
NIHSAD, Bhopal; and  
e)  the details of time taken by laboratories for conducting/completing Avian Influenza Testing 
in these two laboratories and in other such laboratories in the country, State-wise?  
 
 
 ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY & DAIRYING 
 (DR. SANJEEV KUMAR BALYAN) 
 
(a) to (c) Yes sir, migratory birds could be one of the potential sources for introduction of Avian 
Influenza virus into the country. As per World Organization for Animal Health (OIE), wild birds, 
as natural host and reservoir for all types of Avian Influenza viruses, play a major role in the 
evolution, maintenance, and spread of these viruses.  ICAR-National Institute of High Security 
Animal Diseases (NIHSAD), Bhopal has taken up a projec t on “Surveillance of avian influenza 
in wild/ migratory birds”.  As for  the number of  migratory birds visiting various states of the 
country annually, the Department does not maintain any such data. 
 
(d)      Eastern Regional Disease Diagnostic Laboratory (ERDDL), Kolkata is involved in 
testingAvian Influenza for the States/UTs of West Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, Jharkhand, Sikkim and 
Andaman & Nicobar. However, as  an OIE recognized reference laboratory, ICAR -NIHSAD, 
Bhopal provides confirmatory diagnostic services on Avian Influenza to all the States and UTs. 

 
(e)  There are 5 (five) Regional Disease Diagnostic Laboratories (RDDLs) located region-
wise at Bengaluru (Southern), Pune (Western), Jalandhar (Northern), Kolkata (Eastern) and 
Guwahati (North-Eastern) and one Central Disease Diagnostic Laboratory (CDDL) located at 
ICAR-Indian Veterinary Research Institute (IVRI), Izatnagar, Bareilly involved in testing for 
Avian Influenza. However, ICAR-NIHSAD, Bhopal is the National Reference Laboratory for 
confirmation of Avian Influenza.  
 
As per information,ICAR-NIHSAD and the other laboratories provide results for the emergency 
samples received from all states in almost 12-48 hours depending on the time of receipt of the 
eligible samples there.

FUNCTIONING OF BRLF 
 
3248.  SHRI NISITH PRAMANIK: 
DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR: 
SHRIMATI SANGEETA KUMARI SINGH DEO: 
SHRI VINOD KUMAR SONKAR: 
SHRI BHOLA SINGH: 
SHRIMATI SARMISTHA SETHI: 
SHRI RAJA AMARESHWARA NAIK: 
SHRI RAJVEER SINGH (RAJU BAAIYA): 
DR. JAYANTA KUMAR ROY: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Ministry has set up Bharat Rural L ivelihoods Foundation (BRLF) to 
empower rural India; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof including the struc ture, functions and source of budgets; 
(c)  whether the BRLF has been entrusted to ensure better implementation of Government 
schemes in partnership with civil society organizations. 
(d)  if so, whether the BRLF organises various acti vities and programmes for tribals ; 
(e)  if so, the details of achievements made and fu nds sanctioned during the last three years, 
State-wise; 
(f)  whether the Government has reviewed the functi oning of the BRLF; and 
(g)  if so, the steps being taken by the Government  for improvement in the working of the 
BRLF?  
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRI NARENDRA SINGH TOMAR) 
 
(a) to (c):   Bharat Rural Livelihoods Foundation (BRLF)  was set up as  an independent society under 
the Societies Registration Act, 1860 on 03 
rd  December 2013.  BRLF`s mission  is  to facilitate  and 
upscale civil society action in partnership with Go vernment for transforming livelihoods and  lives of  
rural households, with an emphasis on women, Particularly in the Central Indian Tribal Region.  
BRLF is governed by a General Body and Executive Co mmittee comprising elected, nominated or 
ex-officio members. The Secretaries of three Centra l ministries – Rural Development, Tribal Affairs 
and Panchayat Raj are ex-officio members of its Gen eral Body (GB) and Executive Committee (EC).  
GB and  EC also include representatives of state go vernments, eminent persons from academia, civil 

society and the corporate sector with demonstrated experience, understanding and commitment to the 
issues of concern to BRLF, financial institutions, public sector undertakings, philanthropic 
foundations, academic institutions and institutions  representing industry. Presently the President of 
BRLF is Shri Hasmukh Shah, Former Chairman, IPCL.  
BRLF is mandated to provide financial grants to civ il society organizations (CSOs) to meet their 
human resource and institutional costs for up scali ng of proven interventions, invest in institutional  
strengthening of smaller  CSOs and capacity buildin g of professional human resources working at the 
grassroots.  
BRLF  has  two sources for its budget:- (i) corpus and endowment funds wherein only interest earned 
on the funds is utilised for operations and  (ii) g rants and donations  Govt. has provided  BRLF with  
Rs. 200 crore to create its corpus.  BRLF can also partner with private philanthropies, public and 
private sector undertakings seek contribution  to i ts corpus fund or annual grant  or co-financing 
support to the projects funded by it.  
 (d) & (e):  As mentioned above, BRLF engages  with CSOs  and provides  grant suppor t mainly for 
the Human Resources and operations cost of CSOs. In  addition, each CSO supported by BRLF 
attempts to leverage the resources made available b y both banks and government for a number of 
national and/ or state level rural development programmes/ schemes.  
As per information provided by  (BRLF), the following are major achievements made by 
BRLF:-  
 
A. 
BRLF was designated as a Centre of Excellence of Ministry of Tribal Affairs ( MoTA). In 
this role, BRLF has been mandated to  screen  NGOs for MoTA’s Grant-in-Aid Scheme, 
do Research Study on UsharMukti program and evaluate Grant-in-Aid Scheme of MoTA.  
 
B. BRLF supports CSOs to conduct the following capacity building programmes :- 
(i). Certificate Programme in Rural Livelihoods (CP RL) which is a 6-month certificate programme 
targeting the tribal youths of 18-40 years of age. A total of 6 batches with a collective strength of 
174 tribal youths have been launched till date.  
(ii)  BRLF has been providing financial support to bright Adivasi students from the Central India 
Tribal Belt to pursue a two-year MBA in Rural Management from School of Development Studies, 
IIHMRU, Jaipur since 2017. Till now 22 students have been supported to go through this course.  
 (iii) BRLF has supported 25 rural professionals of  tribal areas to receive advanced training on 
‘Water Science and Policy’ in partnership with Shiv Nadar University.  
(iv) BRLF signed an MoU with Jharkhand State Liveli hoods Promotion Society (JSLPS) on 25th 
May 2019 to impart training to 90 Field Thematic Co ordinators to improve current knowledge of 
field staff on contemporary facets of rural livelihoods.  
 
C. Since 2017 BRLF has special thematic partnerships w ith some state governments for 
large scale projects. Highlights of these programs as under:-  
(i). Support to spring rejuvenation program  of Wes t Bangal in four districts   of the State viz., 
Darjeeling, Allipurduar, Kalimpong and Jalpaiguri  for reviving 457 natural springs through 
implementing partners PRASARI and ACWADAM and finan cial support of Arghyam, 
Bangalore.  

(ii). Support to the  “UsharMukti Project” of Govt.  of West Bangal  was launched across 10,091 
villages, 2,080 micro-watersheds, 472 GPs, 55 block s across 6 districts (Purulia, Bankura, 
Jhargram, Birbhum, PaschimMednipur and PaschimBardhaman).  
(iii) . Chhattisgarh Mega Watershed Project: Under the project, an estimated 1,388 Micro-
watersheds are being taken up for area treatment, c hecking soil erosion and runoff reduction 
over 6.94 lakh hectares of land. Under the MoU, the  state government has committed to 
providing Rs1166.4 crores (from MGNREGA) for all tr eatment measures, while BRLF and Axis 
Bank Foundation take care of the CSO facilitation c osts. In terms of administrative sanctions, 
projects worth Rs. 302.15 crores have been sanction ed, of which schemes worth Rs. 135.17 
crores have been completed creating more than 51.4 lakh person-days of employment. 
(iv). Odisha Agriculture Production Cluster Project :  This four year project is a collaborative 
initiative of the Directorate of Horticulture, Odis ha Livelihoods Mission (OLM), BRLF, 
PRADAN and 16 local CSOs to ensure doubling of inco me of 100,000 small and marginal 
farmers especially women by establishing 650 Produc er Groups (PG) aggregated to form 30 
APCs/Producer Company (PCs) in 40 blocks of 12 high land districts. Of these about 64% 
households belong to ST and SC Communities. The est imated cost of the project is INR. 401.60 
crores of which Rs.381 crores is program expenses t o be met out of government contribution 
from different departments, and Rs.20.34 crores is earmarked towards CSO facilitation, being 
borne by BRLF and participating CSOs. Under this pr oject, 790 PGs have been formed covering 
85,167 households and a total of 5509.7 acres of ir rigation potential has been created by 
leveraging resources through different schemes avai lable in the state. Rs. 81.36 crores have been 
leveraged from the state government till September 2020 
(v).. Jharkhand MGNREGA Mega-Watershed Project : BRLF has signed an MoU in August 
2020 with the Rural Development Department of Jharkhand (via MGREGA Commissioner) for a 
mega-watershed project to be implemented across 24 blocks of 6 districts of the state over 4 
years. The project aims at doubling the income of a t least 1 lakh families in these blocks while 
providing water security to 1.91 lakh households an d bringing cropping intensity in 
approximately 1.81 lakh hectares of land. 
(vi). Strengthening Civil Society action in the are as of water, clean energy and climate 
change: The project, being funded by the European Union, is  being implemented in 279 villages 
of 4 blocks in 3 districts of Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand to transform the lives and livelihoods 
of the particularly vulnerable tribal groups and da lits of Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand Under 
this, 1359 water harvesting structures have been co nstructed under MGNREGA and 450-hectare 
land has been brought under protective irrigation. 7448 household have been covered under 
Ujjwala scheme. 1463 houses have constructed under Pradhan MantriAwasYojna and 9922 
farmers from 172 villages supported to adopt sustainable agriculture practices 
(vii). Special Thematic Areas: BRLF has been working on the following special them atic areas 
since inception - Non-Pesticide Management based ag riculture, Participatory Ground Water 
Management, Water and Sanitation, De-notified and N omadic Tribes, Backyard Poultry and 
Farmer Producer Organizations. Special knowledge pa rtners have supported the work of BRLF 
partner CSOs in working on these thematic areas.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. †3249 
 ANSWERED ON 16TH MARCH, 2021 
  
FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES IN ODISHA 
  
†3249. SHRI JUAL ORAM: 
 
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government has any proposal to set up food processing industries in every 
District of Odisha; 
 
(b) if so, the districts in Odisha where food processing zone have already been set up; 
 
(c)  the steps taken to set up food processing zone in the remaining districts of Odisha; and 
 
(d)  the financial assistance provided to the private entrepreneurs to set up such units? 
  
 
 ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI RAMESWAR TELI) 
  
(a) to (d): The Ministry of Food Processing industries (MoFPI) does not setup any food processing 
industries/ units/projects on its own. However, it is implementing a Central Sector umbrella 
scheme- Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana (PMKSY) for overall growth and development of 
food processing sector with an outlay of Rs. 6000 Crore for the period 2016 -17 to 2019 -20. The 
period has since been extended to FY 2020 -21. Under component schemes of PMKSY, MoFPI 
provides mostly credit linke d financial assistance (capital subsidy) in the form of grants -in-aid to 
entrepreneurs for setting up of food processing / preservation industries. PMKSY is not any region 
or state specific but demand driven and is implemented across the country including in the state of 
Odisha.   The details of projects approved in Odisha under the component schemes of PMKSY are 
enclosed at Annexure. 
  
As part of the Aatmanirbhar Bharat Initiative, MoFPI is implementing a Centrally 
Sponsored Scheme-PM Formalisation of Micr o Food Processing Enterprises Scheme (PMFME) 
for providing financial, technical and business support for setting up/upgradation of 2 lakh micro 
food processing enterprises through credit linked subsidy during five years from 2020-21 to 2024-
25 with an outl ay of Rs.10,000 cr.   Out of this, a total of 4709 units have been allocated 
to Odisha with outlay of Rs 215.58 Crores for next five years.
